project: Mock-Backed CLI Run, Status, And Result Loopback For Dynamic Workflows
description: Add the first customer-testable CLI loopback for JavaScript Factory Sessions using the deterministic mock session-provider path. Users can start fixture-backed sessions in synchronous or asynchronous mode, receive durable session ids and inspection links, poll status, retrieve final or partial results, and observe deterministic timeout and failure behavior.

context.customerAsk: Add mock-backed CLI behavior for dynamic workflow run/status/result. A sync run of a fixture returns a completed outcome and expected primary result hash or structured result. An async run returns a durable session id, status links, and later status/result commands report the mock scenario state. Timed-out sync runs report timeout without pretending completion, cancel-on-timeout is visible when requested, and focused CLI tests cover not-ready result, missing session, unsupported mode, bad source, and requestId conflict paths.
context.problem: Dynamic workflow planning has deterministic mock Factory Session provider fixtures and shared execution request/result types, but users still need a CLI surface that proves the run, status, and result loop from their point of view. Without this loopback, downstream runtime and API work cannot demonstrate that you commands normalize inputs consistently, preserve request-id behavior, render stable JSON, or expose session inspection paths for completed, running, timed-out, failed, and not-ready states.
context.solution: Extend CLI command behavior, using existing command boundaries where possible, so run/status/result-style commands call the shared mock-backed Factory Session execution service. Normalize source, args, request id, wait options, cancel-on-timeout, and requested result policy through shared service or API-surface helpers. Render concise human output and deterministic JSON for started, completed, timed-out, running, failed, and not-ready outcomes, with focused CLI tests against deterministic provider fixtures.

acceptanceCriteria: A sync CLI run of the success fixture returns a completed outcome and either the expected primary result hash or the expected structured primary result.
An async CLI run returns a durable Factory Session id, status/result links or follow-up command hints, and later CLI status/result commands report the deterministic mock scenario state.
A sync CLI run that exceeds the wait budget reports a timeout outcome, keeps the session inspectable, and does not render the session as completed.
When cancel-on-timeout is requested, CLI output makes the cancel request or cancellation outcome visible in both human and JSON modes.
CLI JSON output is deterministic for started, completed, timed-out, running, failed, and not-ready result outcomes.
Focused CLI tests cover not-ready result, missing session, unsupported mode, bad source, request-id idempotent replay, and request-id conflict behavior.
Quality gate passes: typecheck, lint where touched, and go test ./pkg/cli/session ./pkg/cli/workflow ./pkg/factorysessionexecution.

userStories.title: Normalize CLI Session Execution Requests
userStories.description: As a CLI user, I want run/status/result commands to interpret source, args, request id, wait options, and result policy consistently so retries and later API parity do not depend on transport-specific rules.
acceptanceCriteria: CLI run input resolves fixture source, args, request id, sync versus async mode, wait timeout, cancel-on-timeout, and requested result policy into the shared Factory Session execution request shape.
Positional arguments, flags, and stdin or file source inputs follow the existing invocation input ownership rules and reject conflicting logical input sources with a clear CLI error.
Unsupported execution modes fail before a session is created and return deterministic human and JSON errors.
Bad or missing source fails before a session is created and returns deterministic human and JSON errors.
Request normalization tests prove equivalent CLI inputs produce the same idempotency tuple used by the mock provider.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Run A Fixture Synchronously To Completion
userStories.description: As a CLI user, I want a synchronous run of a fixture-backed JavaScript Factory Session to return the completed outcome and primary result so I can prove the simplest dynamic workflow path from the terminal.
acceptanceCriteria: A sync run command against the success fixture exits successfully and renders completed or the established terminal success status in human output.
JSON output for the same sync run includes session id, lifecycle/result status, source identity or hash, primary result hash or structured primary result, and inspection links.
The primary result is selected through the shared Factory Session execution or invocation result behavior rather than a CLI-only shortcut.
Re-running the command with the same request id and equivalent inputs returns the original result without creating a new session.
CLI tests assert the completed human output and deterministic JSON fields for the success fixture.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Start A Fixture Asynchronously And Poll Status
userStories.description: As a CLI user, I want to start a fixture-backed JavaScript Factory Session asynchronously and poll its status later so long-running dynamic workflows have an inspectable terminal loop.
acceptanceCriteria: An async run command exits successfully after start and renders a durable Factory Session id plus follow-up status/result links or command hints.
JSON output for async start includes session id, lifecycle status, status/result links, request id when provided, and result availability.
A status command for the returned session id renders the deterministic running, completed, timed-out, or failed mock scenario state.
Status JSON includes lifecycle status, progress or phase summary when available, result availability, dispatch/artifact counts when available, and inspection links.
CLI tests start an async fixture session and then use its returned session id to verify status output from the same mock provider state.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Retrieve Final And Partial Results
userStories.description: As a CLI user, I want result commands to return final results when available and partial or not-ready responses when not available so automation can handle both terminal and in-progress sessions.
acceptanceCriteria: A result command for a completed fixture session renders the expected primary result hash or structured primary result in human and JSON modes.
A result command for a running fixture session returns a not-ready result outcome without treating it as command success with empty data or as an unknown session.
Partial result retrieval, when supported by existing command boundaries, renders available partial data with availability status and stable JSON fields.
Result JSON distinguishes available, not_ready, failed, and missing_session outcomes with deterministic fields and exit behavior appropriate for CLI automation.
CLI tests cover final result, partial or not-ready result, and missing-session result paths against deterministic provider data.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Report Timeout And Cancel-On-Timeout Clearly
userStories.description: As a CLI user, I want a synchronous run that times out to report timeout and optional cancellation explicitly so I do not mistake a live or canceled session for a completed one.
acceptanceCriteria: A sync run with a wait budget smaller than the fixture completion window renders a timeout outcome with session id and status/result inspection links.
Timeout JSON includes lifecycle status, timeout status, result availability, wait duration or timeout flag, and does not include a completed primary result.
When cancel-on-timeout is requested, human output and JSON output include the cancel-on-timeout request and the deterministic cancellation or cancel-submitted outcome from the provider.
A timed-out session remains inspectable through status/result commands unless the deterministic provider scenario reports it as canceled.
CLI tests cover timeout without cancel-on-timeout and timeout with cancel-on-timeout.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: List Dispatches, Artifacts, And Events When Available
userStories.description: As a CLI user, I want inspection commands for dispatches, artifacts, and events to expose deterministic provider data so I can understand what a dynamic workflow session produced.
acceptanceCriteria: Dispatch listing, artifact listing, and event polling commands are added or extended only where existing CLI command boundaries permit a clear session inspection behavior.
Dispatch output includes stable dispatch ids, status, provider session references when present, and owning Factory Session id.
Artifact output includes stable artifact ids, names, metadata or retrieval refs, and owning Factory Session id.
Event polling output includes ordered Factory Session events and supports a cursor or since option when the existing command shape permits it.
JSON output for each supported inspection command is deterministic and matches the mock provider fixture data.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Stabilize CLI Failure And Idempotency Paths
userStories.description: As a CLI maintainer, I want failure and request-id replay paths to be explicit so users get actionable errors and tests protect the loopback contract.
acceptanceCriteria: Missing session status/result requests return clear deterministic CLI errors in human and JSON modes.
Unsupported mode and bad source paths return clear deterministic CLI errors and do not create provider sessions.
Reusing a request id with the same normalized request returns the original start/result behavior.
Reusing a request id with a different normalized request returns a clear request-id conflict error and does not create a new provider session.
Focused CLI tests cover not-ready result, missing session, unsupported mode, bad source, request-id replay, and request-id conflict without relying on real JavaScript runtime or HTTP API.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
